- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >80), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias correction in next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is falling, model underestimates — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if price is trending sharply upward, forecast often peaks too early — reduce forecast slope after 3–5 consecutive rising days.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from positive to negative) triggers model lag — delay forecast adjustment until sentiment stabilizes or confirms new trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility — use 18-day history as anchor, not 30-day trend, to avoid overreaction to short-term noise.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is flat, model tends to drift — apply small downward bias to avoid false continuation.
